headline: Learned generative models couple biological priors to causal single-cell inference
label: Single Cell Generative Modeling
summary: Recent preprints and papers pair latent-variable and graph architectures with perturbation, regulatory, and lineage structure in single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generative and latent-variable architectures that encode explicit biological structure, such as regulatory graphs, metabolic topology, lineage trees, and cell-cell interaction networks, coupled to causal or dynamical inference. Perturbation prediction recurs across several items: scEGFlow applies energy-guided flow matching to move cells from control to perturbed states, PerturbBridge models responses as latent Schrödinger Bridge transport, and SHERLOCK treats perturbation effects as latent interventions. Regulatory work includes DeepSCENIC, which transfers sequence-to-function enhancer models to multiome data for causal GRN inference, and SPECTRA, which propagates CRISPRi effects through directed graph neural networks. scPFA models latent programs evolving along lineage trees, while Speciesformer adds cross-species pretraining on 131M cells from 11 species. The shared novelty is tying such priors to causal or dynamical inference rather than descriptive embedding alone.
